source_name: ECB Banking Supervision – List of supervised entities (SSM)
why_relevant: Authoritative periodic list separating significant institutions (directly ECB-supervised, e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka) from less significant ones supervised by NBS. Determines which supervisory channel and which resolution authority (SRB vs Rezolučná rada) publishes about each SK bank — the routing key for this whole cell.

source_name: Single Resolution Board (SRB) – MREL dashboards
why_relevant: Quarterly MREL dashboards covering all SRB-remit banks, including the SK significant institutions. Reports MREL targets, outstanding stock, shortfalls (external and internal MREL) and issuance/cost-of-funding trends. Complements the national Rezolučná rada channel, which handles institutions outside the SRB remit. SRB also publishes SK-language explanatory material.

source_name: Centrálny register zmlúv (CRZ) – contracts of FOV and public-sector financial bodies
why_relevant: Mandatory Slovak public contracts register. Reveals-indirectly: procurement and service contracts of the Deposit Protection Fund (and other public financial bodies) expose vendors, IT systems, payout-agent arrangements and audit engagements that never appear in the annual report.

source_name: MF SR – Účtovníctvo pre Fond ochrany vkladov a Garančný fond investícií (accounting decrees)
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance decrees (e.g. MF/22273/2008-74) that define the layout, item content and the disclosable scope of FOV/GFI financial statements. The schema definition behind the annual-report tables — essential for building a stable parser and for knowing when a template change is coming.

source_name: Banky.sk – zoznam bánk na Slovensku (bank directory)
why_relevant: Non-official but convenient SK-language directory of every bank and branch operating in Slovakia, with per-bank pages. Useful as a cross-check against the NBS register when building the disclosure-crawl seed list, and it surfaces smaller institutions (e.g. Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka) that dominate no search results.

source_name: NBS – Subjekty finančného trhu (financial market entities database)
why_relevant: Master NBS register of all supervised entities, with a dedicated sector 'Bankovníctvo, platobné služby a elektronické peniaze' covering platobné inštitúcie and inštitúcie elektronických peňazí. This is the entry pointer that converts an invisible payments landscape into a named actor list; it also offers a 'Databáza na stiahnutie' bulk download.

source_name: NBS PSD2 register – JSON API (subjekty.nbs.sk/api/psd2)
why_relevant: Machine-readable daily-refreshed feed of Slovak payment service providers (PI, EMI, AISP/PISP/PIISP, banks). Returns business name, address, IČO and licence scope — the cheapest structured way to keep the SK payments actor map current and to detect new licences/withdrawals. A digitally signed variant and a code-list endpoint exist alongside it.

source_name: NBS – Platobné inštitúcie a AISP (supervision section)
why_relevant: Regulator's definitional/licensing page for payment institutions and account information service providers, with links to the entity list. Useful for taxonomy, capital thresholds and for the Slovak/English term mapping needed when searching.

source_name: NBS – Inštitúcie elektronických peňazí / Electronic money institutions
why_relevant: Defines the EMI and 'EMI to a limited extent' categories and their capital requirements (EUR 350k), and links to the list of authorised issuers of electronic money. Necessary to distinguish full EMIs from limited-scope registrations when building the SK e-money actor map.

source_name: Trust Pay, a. s. – corporate documents page
why_relevant: Bratislava-based licensed Slovak payment institution and one of the largest SK-domiciled cross-border acquirers/PSPs. Its documents section carries accounting statements (IFRS individual statements referenced for FY ending 30 Sep 2024), terms and regulatory disclosures — a genuine first-party disclosure source in this cell.

source_name: SKPAY, a. s. – corporate site and product disclosures
why_relevant: Slovak payment AND e-money institution founded 2012 as a joint venture of Slovenská pošta and Poštová banka; operates post-office payment services and card acceptance (mojapos.skpay.sk). Publishes product/company information PDFs and is a rare SK-domiciled EMI with retail distribution reach.

source_name: EVERIFIN s. r. o. – Slovak open-banking PISP/AISP
why_relevant: Trnava-based Slovak fintech licensed by NBS as AISP/PISP (appears in the NBS PSD2 feed), operating a pan-European open-banking payment platform (PayGate, retail payments). Its blog/news section is a live signal channel for SK A2A payment adoption; financials retrievable via RÚZ.

source_name: Global Payments s.r.o. (Slovensko) – acquirer site and newsroom
why_relevant: Active in Slovakia since 2016 as a card-acceptance/terminal and payment-gateway provider; in Oct 2025 launched its own cashless-payment solution ahead of the state scheme, generating trade coverage. Local-entity financials are filed in RÚZ even though group results are reported by the US parent.

source_name: EBA Payment Institutions Register (EUCLID PIR)
why_relevant: EU-wide 'golden copy' of PSD2 payment and e-money institutions, including passporting: identifies EEA firms that have notified services INTO Slovakia and SK firms passporting out. This is the only systematic way to see the passported layer of the SK payments market, which the national register alone understates.

source_name: Banco de España – list of payment-statistics relevant institutions, Slovakia
why_relevant: ESCB-derived PSRI list for Slovakia: an independently maintained roster of SK payment service providers relevant for payment statistics. Useful as a cross-check on the NBS register and to catch entities classified differently by the statistical framework.

source_name: MF SR – vzory tlačív pre platobné inštitúcie a inštitúcie elektronických peňazí
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance publishes the mandatory financial-statement templates that SK payment and e-money institutions must use. Knowing the exact statement schema makes automated parsing of RÚZ filings for this cell tractable rather than ad hoc.

source_name: Slovenská Fintech asociácia (Slovak Fintech Association)
why_relevant: Industry body for SK fintech/payments firms; its membership list is a snowball source for payment institutions and EMIs that never appear in bank-centric coverage, and its positions/news reveal regulatory pressure points. Complements the NBS register with the pre-licence and adjacent-player layer.

source_name: FinReport.sk – Slovak finance trade portal
why_relevant: Publishes analytic pieces and press releases on SK payment-market policy and providers (e.g. readiness for mandatory cashless payments, Oct 2025). A useful secondary channel for PI/EMI announcements that lack their own newsroom.

source_name: SITA – firmy a inštitúcie (corporate press-release wire)
why_relevant: Slovak news agency that hosts per-organisation press-release streams (confirmed for Slovenská banková asociácia). Payment institutions and financial associations distribute tlačové správy here, so it works as a per-actor release archive for firms with no newsroom of their own.

source_name: Slovenská pošta – SKPAY service page
why_relevant: State-owned Slovenská pošta documents SKPAY's role as the payment/e-money institution behind post-office payment services, revealing the distribution and ownership structure of a major SK EMI. Slovenská pošta's own annual report is an indirect window on SKPAY volumes.

source_name: Global Payments Slovensko - corporate site (globalpayments.sk)
why_relevant: Slovak-market site of the dominant merchant acquirer in SK (Global Payments / Erste-Slovenska sporitelna JV). Carries product launches, terminal/POS portfolio, partner programme and the 'Dolezite dokumenty' page with acceptance contract terms and pricing conditions - the closest thing to SK-level acquiring disclosure.

source_name: Global Payments Inc. - Investor Relations / SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K)
why_relevant: Parent-level disclosure of the SK acquiring JV. The 2015 8-K/10-K documented the CaixaBank/Erste Group venture covering Czech Republic, Slovakia and Romania (51/49 split, EUR 30m). Segment 'Europe' commentary and any JV restructuring/impairment is where SK acquiring economics surface.

source_name: Slovenska sporitelna - Global Payments partner page (biznis/globalpayments)
why_relevant: Bank side of the acquiring JV. Documents which acceptance products SLSP distributes, pricing bundles and terminal offers - lets you infer the SK acquiring value chain and any change of partner/branding without acquirer disclosure.

source_name: Nexi Central Europe, a.s. - corporate site (ex SIA Central Europe, ex First Data Slovakia)
why_relevant: The main card processor legally domiciled in Bratislava (Rontgenova 1), ICO 31372074, serving SK/CZ/HR/HU/RS. Direct successor of the First Data CEE processing estate acquired by SIA, then Nexi. Full issuing+acquiring processing, terminal management, VAS - the processing-infrastructure anchor for the SK cell.

source_name: Nexi Group Investor Relations - integrated annual report & quarterly results (CSEE segment)
why_relevant: Nexi reports a 'Central and Southeastern Europe (CSEE)' segment (~15% of group revenue, EUR 258m in H1 2026) which contains Slovakia. Segment revenue/volume commentary and any SK bank-contract wins/losses are disclosed here and nowhere in Slovak filings.

source_name: Worldline Investor Relations - financial press releases archive
why_relevant: Worldline is active in SK merchant acquiring (worldline.com/sk-sk). Group FY/H1 results releases carry Merchant Services regional commentary, contract wins and divestments; SK exposure only ever appears at this level.

source_name: Worldline Slovensko - local market site (sk-sk)
why_relevant: Slovak-language storefront of Worldline: terminal portfolio (Axium DX8000), Tap on Mobile, acquiring/issuing/ATM management. Confirms actual SK market presence and product positioning versus Global Payments.

source_name: chcemterminal.sk - Worldline SK distribution/lead site
why_relevant: Local reseller/marketing front for Worldline terminals in SK. Useful for observing pricing, promo terms and channel partners that never appear in group disclosure.
